post.description: ActivityPub inbox of one Profile actor. NOT MOUNTED on the production router (the production mount is owned by the P4 cutover). Requires a valid HTTP Signature whose key owner is `activity.actor`. Received activity table: Follow (object = this Profile; stored as an accepted generation and an Accept delivery job is reserved in the same transaction; when the Profile blocks the signer the Follow is refused instead: an ended generation is stored and a Reject(Follow) delivery job is reserved), Accept / Reject (object = a Follow this Profile sent, matched by the original Follow activity ID and by both parties), Undo (object = a Follow of the signer; an Undo that overtakes its Follow is remembered so the late Follow creates nothing). Every other activity (post activities such as Create / Like / EmojiReact / Announce, Block, Undo of a non-Follow, ...) is acknowledged with 202 and changes nothing: post authorization belongs to ShuttlePub and domain policy to D8G. Stale (ended generation), foreign (other Profile / other actor), unknown-Follow and duplicate activities are acknowledged with 202 without changing any relation.

408.description: The follower actor could not be resolved (retryable)

422.description: Activity violates the Profile inbox rules (wrong target Profile, malformed reference)

get.description: Readiness of each registration protection (email via SMTP, bot via Turnstile), evaluated at the current time against the current configuration. `status` is `operational` only while a real verification business success bound to the current configuration `generation` is fresh (`valid_until`); health, HTTP 200 or an SMTP 250 alone never make a protection operational. `unverified` covers never verified, configuration changed, success expired and probe stopped. `configuration_invalid` covers unset/empty/disabled configuration, invalid secrets and SMTP auth/configuration failures; `temporarily_unavailable` covers 429/5xx/timeouts/connection failures/SMTP 4xx. Secrets, tokens, proofs and registrant emails never appear; `fingerprint` is a short non-reversible digest of the secret.

post.description: Run one real verification now (bootstrap or re-verification) and record both the business result and the transport classification. bot: with `token` (a valid token issued by the widget for the configured site key) the real Siteverify business result decides (success must match the expected hostname/action and be fresh); without it only a negative probe runs (confirms the secret is accepted, never makes the protection operational). email: without `challenge_id`/`code` an SMTP connection/auth probe runs and a code is sent to the approved canary mailbox (REGISTRATION_EMAIL_CANARY_ADDRESS; `canary_not_configured` leaves the protection unverified); with `challenge_id` and `code` the canary roundtrip is confirmed, which is the business success. A canary confirmation never issues a registration proof. A user-attributable rejection (`attempt_rejected`, for example a wrong code or an invalid token) is reported but not recorded and does not change the gate observation. Recorded results update the registration gate observation through the E15a use case.

get.description: Webhook delivery status: whether the external Webhook is configured (`not_configured` means it is disabled, which is not an error: nothing is delivered and the gate is unaffected), a misconfiguration classification, the destination host only (never userinfo, path, query or the signing secret), delivery counts, the last success/failure times and the most recent delivery records. Delivery guarantees: at-least-once (the same event can arrive more than once after a retry, a crash or an admin retry, so receivers must de-duplicate by the stable event ID), no ordering guarantee, signed with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp and body. The endpoint and secret are server configuration only and cannot be changed through the API. Delivery runs outside the gate state transition: Webhook failures never change the gate and never create new notification events.

post.description: Requeue failed deliveries so they are sent again with the same event ID (at-least-once: the receiver may see the event more than once). With `event_id`, only that failed delivery is requeued (404 if it is not currently failed); without it, every failed delivery is requeued. Failed deliveries are never retried automatically.

404.description: No failed delivery with that event ID

post.description: Send one synthetic `webhook_test` event (event ID prefixed `test_`) to the configured endpoint through the same path as real deliveries (signature, destination check, timeout) and return the result. The test is a single attempt: it is not retried and no delivery record is stored. It never changes the gate state, the notification list or unread counts. Returns 409 when the Webhook is not configured or misconfigured (nothing is sent).

200.description: Test sent; `delivered` tells whether the receiver answered 2xx

409.description: Webhook is not configured or misconfigured

get.description:
Check whether a Profile username could be assigned, for input-time validation. The answer is ADVISORY: it is a snapshot, nothing is reserved (no hold), and another request may take the username before the form is submitted, so the final decision is always made by the create / set username APIs (400 for a malformed or reserved value, 409 when the username is taken).

The rules are the same as those applied by the create / set username APIs: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` (ASCII lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; 1-64 characters), a reserved-word list, and no implicit conversion (no trimming or case folding: `Alice` is `invalid_format`, not `alice`). A username is unique across all Profiles, also deleted ones, and is never reused.

Always 200 for a well-formed request: `available` is true, or false with `reason` = `invalid_format`, `reserved` or `taken`. `taken` covers both "in use" and "used by a deleted Profile" and does not tell them apart (so the response reveals neither whether a Profile was deleted nor anything else about its owner). A missing `username` parameter is 400. Read-only: nothing is created or stored.

Rate limited per authenticated caller (token `iss` + `sub`): 60 requests per minute, then 429 with `Retry-After` (seconds). The limit is kept in memory per server instance and is not shared between instances. Changing a username is not supported.

429.description: Too many checks; see the Retry-After header (seconds)

post.description: Unauthenticated. Start a pre-registration email ownership challenge: a one-time code is sent to the address and bound to the normalized email, the real registration flow (flow_id) and the current configuration generation. Sending the mail is NOT proof of ownership; a proof is issued only after the code is confirmed (see `/confirm`). Abuse controls: the code is sent only while the registration gate accepts registrations and the email protection is operational (otherwise 503 and nothing is sent), per-email (1 per 60 s, 5 per hour), per-flow (3 per hour) and per-source (connection address, default 20 per hour) rate limits answer 429 with Retry-After. The response does not depend on whether the address exists, is registered or was rejected by the mail server (no user enumeration). The challenge expires after 10 minutes (never later than the flow) and allows 5 confirmation attempts. The flow is checked against Kratos (existence and its real expiry). A browser flow can only be checked with its Kratos CSRF cookie (`csrf_token_*`), so send this request with the browser credentials (cookies) for the Kratos domain; only those cookies are forwarded to Kratos. A flow whose expiry cannot be confirmed is rejected (400), never guessed.

202.description: Challenge created (a code is sent to the address)

503.description: Email verification is unavailable; nothing was sent

post.description: Unauthenticated. Confirm the emailed code. Only a correct code issues an opaque `proof` (shown once), bound to the challenge's flow, email and configuration generation, valid for 15 minutes (never later than the flow). The proof is passed to registration as `transient_payload.email_proof` and verified and consumed atomically by the registration hook (E15d); it is never a permission on its own. A wrong code consumes one of 5 attempts (the challenge is invalidated afterwards). Unknown challenge, wrong code, expired, exhausted and old-generation challenges are indistinguishable (400).

parameters.description: Challenge ID returned by the create endpoint

400.description: Invalid request, or the code is invalid or expired

tags.name: ProfileActor
tags.description: Profile ActivityPub actor document and inbox (1 Profile = 1 actor). The actor generation logic (P1) and the inbox (P3i: Follow / Accept / Reject / Undo(Follow)) exist but the routes are NOT MOUNTED on the production router before the P4 cutover.

tags.name: ProfilePolicy
tags.description: CONTRACT ONLY, not mounted on the production router (mounted in P4 at the earliest): Profile identity, Profile-scoped follow, individual block/mute and domain-controls. Handlers answer 501 until P3o/D8G/D8R implement them, except domain-controls (D8P: stored, revision-controlled, owner-only) and followers/following (P3i: read from the P2 follow graph, owner-only), which are implemented but stay unmounted on the production router until P4/D8R. Owner-only authorization, revision conflicts (409) and errors are the contract.

tags.name: RegistrationGate
tags.description: Registration readiness gate (admin only). The authenticated Kratos pre-persist hook enforces gate decisions. Enforcement attestation loss stops registration ahead of override; restoration requires manual resume. Emumet cannot physically block a Kratos deployment with the hook removed; finite canary sampling cannot cover unknown or unselected replicas. Physical containment is the deployment operator's responsibility.

tags.name: RegistrationGateWebhook
tags.description: External Webhook delivery of registration gate notification events (admin only; E15w). The endpoint URL and the HMAC-SHA256 signing secret are server configuration only (REGISTRATION_WEBHOOK_URL, REGISTRATION_WEBHOOK_SECRET or REGISTRATION_WEBHOOK_SECRET_FILE). When they are unset the Webhook is disabled: nothing is delivered, the status endpoint reports `not_configured`, and the gate is unaffected (this is not an error). Delivery guarantees: at-least-once, so the same event can be delivered more than once (retries, crash recovery, admin retry) and receivers must de-duplicate by the stable event ID (`X-Emumet-Event-Id`); ordering is not guaranteed (order by `occurred_at` if needed). Retries: 408/429/5xx/timeouts/connection failures are retried with exponential backoff and jitter (Retry-After is honored up to a cap) until the attempt or age limit, then the delivery is `failed`; redirects, other 4xx responses and destination-check (SSRF) rejections fail immediately. Failed deliveries are resent only when an admin requests a retry. Webhook trouble never changes the gate state and never creates a new notification event. HTTPS only, no redirects, destinations are checked at connect time and pinned. Receiver documentation: docs/registration-gate-webhook.md.

tags.name: RegistrationProtection
tags.description: Registration protection readiness and pre-registration email proof (E15c). Unauthenticated: POST /api/v1/registration/email-challenges and /confirm (email ownership challenge: code by SMTP, proof only after the code is confirmed; rate limited; bound to flow, email and configuration generation). Admin only: GET /api/v1/admin/registration-gate/protections and POST /api/v1/admin/registration-gate/protections/{protection}/verify (readiness and real verification). Configuration is server-side only (REGISTRATION_TURNSTILE_*, REGISTRATION_SMTP_*, REGISTRATION_EMAIL_*). A protection is operational only while a real verification business success bound to the current configuration generation is fresh; health, HTTP 200 and SMTP 250 alone never make it operational. The authenticated production Kratos pre-persist hook consumes these proofs and tokens; client readiness results never authorize registration by themselves. Operations guide: docs/registration-protection-readiness.md.
